headline: Wilderness Permit and Remote Logistical Planning
reservation: Access requires mandatory registration and nightly camping fees at North Maine Woods gatehouses like Telos or Churchill Dam. While there is no lottery, campsites are first-come, first-served, and groups over 12 must follow specific capacity limits. Verify current gate status and logging road conditions via official Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands channels.

days.title: Paddling the Great Lakes

stops.name: Chamberlain Lake
stops.detail: Navigate the largest lake in the waterway, being mindful of wind-driven waves that can challenge loaded canoes.

stops.name: Eagle Lake Tramway
stops.detail: Walk to the site of 20th-century steam locomotives abandoned in the woods, a relic of the region's logging history.

days.driving: Local transfer by water; allow 5–7 hours of paddling depending on wind.
days.note: Lakes can become dangerous in high winds; stay close to the shoreline.

days.title: Rapids and River Relics

stops.name: Chase Rapids
stops.detail: Maneuver through Class II whitewater; use the ranger-led portage service for gear if you prefer a lighter boat.

stops.name: Umsaskis Lake
stops.detail: Transition back to calm water for wildlife viewing, looking for moose grazing along the marshy banks.

days.driving: Local transfer by water; allow 4–6 hours for river travel.
days.note: Water levels at Chase Rapids are controlled by dam releases; check daily flows with the ranger.

days.title: Vistas and Valley Floats

stops.name: Allagash Mountain
stops.detail: Hike to the fire tower at the summit for a 360-degree view of the Maine North Woods and distant peaks.

stops.name: Round Pond
stops.detail: Paddle into this quiet basin, an excellent area for spotting bald eagles and hearing loon calls.

days.driving: Local transfer by water; allow 5 hours for the pond transition and hike.
days.note: The trail to the fire tower is moderately steep; allow 2 hours for the round-trip hike.

intel.title: Private Logging Roads
intel.text: Access is via private logging roads where timber trucks have the right of way. Check for active harvesting closures and road washouts before departing gateway towns.

intel.title: The Last Stop
intel.text: No fuel or supplies exist within the 92-mile waterway. Fully stock all provisions and fuel in Fort Kent or Millinocket before passing the entry gates.

intel.title: Total Disconnect
intel.text: There is no cellular service or public Wi-Fi within the wilderness area. Carry a satellite communication device for emergencies and notify a third party of your float plan.

intel.title: Remote Launches
intel.text: Parking is limited to designated dirt pull-offs at entry points like Telos. Arrange a commercial shuttle to move your vehicle to the northern takeout to avoid a long return drive.

intel.title: Campsite Selection
intel.text: Since sites are not reservable, aim to be off the water by 3 PM. Popular spots near historic ruins fill early during the July and August peak.

plan.arrival: Fly into Bangor, rent a high-clearance vehicle, and drive 4 hours to the North Maine Woods gate for registration and fee payment.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance SUVs or trucks with full-size spares are recommended for rugged gravel logging roads; verify rental insurance for unpaved surfaces.
plan.goldenHour: The shoreline of Eagle Lake for a sunset view over the water; seasonal morning mist often creates dramatic lighting.
